subject: Contract rollover — proposed term & capacity amendments
messages:
From: Sofia Kramer <sofia.kramer@acme-ai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: 2028-11-28T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Contract rollover — initial proposal for term + capacity

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team liked the throughput numbers and the burst plan. We're ready to move forward with a 24-month rollover but need to align a few legal/ops items before procurement signs. High-level asks from Acme: 

- Extend current MSA term from 12 -> 24 months (rollover effective 2029-01-01)
- Add a 30% capacity uplift across Exhibit C (starting month 1 of the rollover) with an option to true-up after 90 days
- Move billing to quarterly-in-advance (current monthly-in-arrears)
- Short carveout in Section 9 for data residency (EU-only controls for certain workloads) — we have a draft from our counsel and will share it if helpful

I attached our redline and the updated capacity table for reference (see ACME_Rollover_Proposed_Changes_v2.docx and ExhibitC-capacity-table.xlsx). Can you confirm Redwood's position on: SLA credits for multi-region failover, whether the true-up can be automated, and whether you can accept quarterly-in-advance billing?

If it's easier, let's do a quick 30-min call Monday to walk through the high-impact items and hand off legal redlines.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Kramer
Head of Platform Procurement — Acme AI
sofia.kramer@acme-ai.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Kramer <sofia.kramer@acme-ai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-29T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Contract rollover — initial proposal for term + capacity

Sofia — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We're excited to keep Acme on Redwood. Quick thoughts up front: 

- Term: 24 months is feasible from a commercial perspective; we do want to align on early-termination provisions (specifically whether either party can terminate for convenience within the first 12 months without a pro-rata settlement).
- Capacity uplift: We can accommodate a 30% uplift; recommend a 90-day usage true-up mechanism tied to Exhibit C (automated via usage reports + agreed measurement windows).
- Billing cadence: Quarterly-in-advance is doable for enterprise deals — will need to confirm finance approval for the billing change and update Exhibit B (billing terms).
- SLA credits & multi-region failover: We can include an explicit failover SLO with credit amounts capped at X% of quarterly fees — I'll loop Ben and Mateo for the exact SLO language.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Internal review: Ben will confirm pricing and credit caps; Mateo to produce an MSA redline responding to the termination and data residency asks.
2) Touchpoint: 30-min alignment call Tues 11/30 11:00am PT — is that OK?

I'll attach a brief checklist for the legal redline to make sure we converge quickly.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-11-30T12:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Contract rollover — initial proposal for term + capacity

Sofia / team — quick commercial response: 

- Pricing: 30% uplift on capacity maps to a blended ARR delta of $420k annually based on current usage. We can provide a 90-day price protection clause for the rates in the rollover (i.e., no price increases for the first 90 days post-execution).
- SLA credits: propose a tiered credit schedule tied to incident severity and time-to-recovery for multi-region failover. Cap the total credits to 25% of the affected quarter's fees.
- Quarterly-in-advance: Finance flagged that they'll need a PO + signed SOW before invoice. We'll note this in Exhibit B.

Action items from my side: update pricing schedule and draft a short 90-day price protection clause for inclusion in the order form.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

--- On a related note (internal): Mateo, can you review the proposed termination-for-convenience language? We should avoid open-ended pro-rata refunds in the first 12 months.

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Sofia Kramer <sofia.kramer@acme-ai.com>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-12-04T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Contract rollover — initial proposal for term + capacity

Hi all — attaching a tracked MSA redline (MSA-redline-annotated.pdf) with the following high-level positions: 

- Term / Termination: We can accept a 24-month term but propose a limited termination-for-convenience window (months 13–24 only). For the first 12 months, termination would be allowed only for material breach or insolvency; if Acme requires termination for convenience earlier, Redwood requests a pro-rata invoice for unused pre-paid quarters plus an early-termination fee equal to 15% of remaining committed fees.

- Billing change: Amend Exhibit B to reflect quarterly-in-advance. Insert PO requirement and billing contact. Finance requires net-30 after invoice for credits only; otherwise invoices due on receipt for pre-paid quarters.

- Exhibit C (capacity): Insert automated true-up process: monthly usage snapshots, 90-day reconciliation window, and a one-time true-up invoice/credit. Also added a clause for burst pool prioritization and overage rates (pre-agreed).

- Data residency: Acme's draft carveout is mostly acceptable; clarified encryption-in-transit and at-rest obligations and added a 30-day remediation SLA for any confirmed cross-border processing incidents.

- SLA credits: Added explicit calculation method and capped total credits per quarter. Added an expedited incident escalation path that triggers additional monitoring support.

Next steps: Sofia / Acme legal to review the PDF redline and revert with any counterpoints. If acceptable, we can produce a clean order form and route for signature via DocuSign.

Mateo Alvarez
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachment: MSA-redline-annotated.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Rossi <erossi@mplaw.com>

Date: 2028-12-11T16:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Contract rollover — initial proposal for term + capacity

Mateo / Kimberly — thanks for the redline. Acme legal has reviewed MSA-redline-annotated.pdf and proposed three narrow edits: 

1) Move the early-termination fee to a flat schedule (we proposed 10% instead of 15%) and narrow the definition of "remaining committed fees" to exclude credits applied for prior incidents.
2) Clarify the billing PO flow: Acme will provide a standing PO number that Redwood can reference on quarterly invoices; any change to the PO will be communicated 30 days in advance.
3) Data residency: request explicit language that Redwood will not transfer dataset X (regulated PII bucket) out of EU control planes without written consent. We suggested a short annex rather than modifying Section 9 directly.

We attached our counter-redline to the Doc (ACME_Rollover_Proposed_Changes_v2.docx) and a clean Exhibit C with the capacity table marked in green. If Redwood accepts the edits above, Acme is prepared to sign once a final SOW and order form are produced.

Proposed next step: mutual acceptance of the three items above and then route documents to DocuSign.

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Partner — Morgan & Park LLP (counsel to Acme AI)
erossi@mplaw.com
